name: Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors v. Superior Court
summary: The ACLU sought records of the county's settlement payments in police misconduct cases. The county withheld communications between county employees and the county counsel's office, claiming attorney-client privilege under § 6254(k) (now § 7923.700). The California Supreme Court held that the attorney-client privilege protects confidential attorney-client communications from CPRA disclosure, but the government may not use privilege to shield records of its own misconduct.
holding: Government Code § 6254(k) (now § 7923.700) incorporates the attorney-client privilege and attorney work-product doctrine as exemptions to CPRA. Confidential communications between a government agency and its attorneys are exempt from disclosure. However, the privilege does not protect facts underlying the representation or documents prepared for purposes other than legal advice.

legal_definitions.definition: Section 6254(k) / 7923.700 incorporates the attorney-client privilege, exempting from CPRA disclosure any confidential communication between a client and their lawyer. For government agencies, communications with in-house and outside counsel for the purpose of legal advice are protected.
legal_definitions.context: The court resolved tension between CPRA access and attorney-client privilege in favor of privilege for bona fide confidential attorney communications.

relevance_to_audit: Defines the scope of § 6254(k) / § 7923.700 attorney-client exemption. Relevant when agencies withhold records claiming attorney-client privilege — ODIA L-3 must verify that the claim applies only to actual confidential attorney communications, not to factual records or business documents routed through counsel.

key_quotes.text: Government agencies may invoke the attorney-client privilege to protect confidential communications with their attorneys, but they may not use the privilege as a shield to prevent disclosure of underlying facts or records that would otherwise be subject to CPRA.
key_quotes.context: Limiting the scope of the § 6254(k) exemption to actual attorney-client communications.

procedural_posture: Writ of mandate; Court of Appeal denied; reversed in part
subsequent_treatment: Controlling authority on attorney-client privilege under CPRA; widely cited by local agencies and media organizations
